task_instance: Created a points.csv with 5 known GPS coordinates (New York, London, Tokyo, Sydney, Paris), installed the reverse_geocoder Python package, and used it to reverse-geocode each point to nearest city, admin region, and country code, writing points_geocoded.csv.
evidence: pip3 install --user reverse_geocoder succeeded (built wheel from source, using existing numpy/scipy). Wrote geocode.py which calls reverse_geocoder.search() on coordinates parsed from points.csv and writes points_geocoded.csv with columns id,lat,lon,city,admin1,cc. Ran `python3 geocode.py` which printed 'Loading formatted geocoded file...' then 'done' (reverse_geocoder builds/loads its bundled GeoNames KD-tree locally, no network calls made). Verified output via `cat points_geocoded.csv`: 40.7128,-74.0060 -> New York City, New York, US; 51.5074,-0.1278 -> London, England, GB; 35.6895,139.6917 -> Tokyo, Tokyo, JP; -33.8688,151.2093 -> Sydney, New South Wales, AU; 48.8566,2.3522 -> Paris, Ile-de-France, FR. All results correct, confirming the offline reverse-geocoding deliverable works as specified.
